title: repair_mesh leaves zero faces showing their back outside on every crawfish scan: outer-surface stage for folds, flaps, doubled caps and sagging fills
user-messages:
> I’d recommend option 2: the orientation fix is a clear improvement on every scan, and the outside-surface step is its own design job. Also, should “no flipped normals” mean no cyan visible in renders of each scan, or literally zero faces by the count above? The count includes single specks you can’t see in a render.

yes , and yes should be zero in the follow on ticket by checking script not from render check
description:
Follow-up to CRAW-91, which made repair_mesh's orient stage turn a folded-through sheet (IMG_4113's eyes) outward by which side of each face sees out to infinity. After it, every crawfish scan still has faces whose back, not front, faces the outside, in four classes orientation alone cannot fix:

1. Thin flaps and sheets with open space on both sides (IMG_4117 about 5,250 faces, IMG_4118 about 780): either winding shows a back to one side.
2. Doubled caps: turning a fold outward means cutting its seam to the skin, which leaves two boundary loops along one curve; fillHoles fills both, so two coincident fills with opposite windings overlap and one always shows its back (the speckled ring round each IMG_4113 eye; reproduced by MeshRepairTest.aChamberFoldedOutThroughTheSkinIsTurnedToFaceOut, whose floor fill is excluded there for this ticket).
3. Faired fills (MeshHoleFiller) sagging out through the skin. CRAW-91 tried refilling such loops flat (fairing off, then refinement off) when a fill showed its back outside: 4113's back-out fill faces went 778 -> 412, but repair_mesh time doubled on 4113, so it did not land.
4. Small inside-out patches whose seams outweigh their own exposure evidence.

Zero needs a stage that keeps only the outer surface: remove interior and folded sheets and flaps and re-close, e.g. generalized winding numbers (Jacobson, Kavan, Sorkine-Hornung 2013, "Robust Inside-Outside Segmentation using Generalized Winding Numbers") or mesh arrangements (Zhou, Grinspun, Zorin, Jacobson 2016, "Mesh Arrangements for Solid Geometry"). Read the paper before designing the stage. Port only permissively licensed code (libigl's winding number code is MPL2 — check before reading).

The check is a script, not a render: per scan, cast from each output face of repair_mesh along its normal both ways against the whole output (BVH nearest hit), and count faces whose back ray escapes and whose front ray does not, plus faces whose both rays escape (flaps). CRAW-91's per-scan numbers with this measure are on that ticket.
definition-of-done:
1. A checking script (ixdar-cli command or benchmark test) reports, for each of IMG_4109-4118 after repair_mesh with the scan DSLs' settings, the faces whose back alone sees out and the faces that see out on both sides; both are exactly 0 on all ten scans.
2. The script is in the repo and its output for all ten scans is recorded on the ticket.
3. Reference ring fingerprints for IMG_4109-4111 reported before/after, any change explained.
4. repair_mesh time per scan reported before/after.

Keeps the [orientation] lines of CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark: they are the per-scan report item 1 asks the checking script for.

Keeps [orientation] total backOut: the checking script's all-scan total.

Keeps exposedFaceCount, prunedFaceCount, pruneRoundCount, refilledHoleCount and refillOpenHoleCount: the pruning stage's counts in the repair report, beside every other stage's.

Keeps the [cold-repair] lines and the child JVM's System.out time line of CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark, and its forwarding of the child's output through Platforms.log: the benchmark reports each scan's first repair in a fresh JVM, the cold time CRAW-93 is judged by.

Keeps Platforms.log(line + System.lineSeparator()); and System.out.println(TIME_PREFIX + (System.nanoTime() - start) in CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark: the child JVM prints its repair time and the parent forwards the child's output.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test -Dtest=MeshRepairTest.
2. The checking script over IMG_4109-4118.
changes-made: Checking script: ixdar-app/test/benchmark/CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark.java (mvn test -Dtest=CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark -Dixdar.test.heap='-Xmx8g [-Dbenchmark.scans=IMG_4113,...]'); one centroid ray along and against each repaired triangle's normal, nearest hit over the whole output. Baseline on CRAW-91 (back-out / flaps): 4109 16/0, 4110 327/5, 4111 197/2, 4112 265/18, 4113 1455/21, 4114 371/0, 4115 267/17, 4116 539/14, 4117 5572/1133, 4118 815/125; total 9824/1335, a third to a half of them fill faces. Every output is closed and consistently wound (0 open holes, 0 boundary, 0 unoriented edges), so a flap means an overlapping sheet within the 1e-6 minimum ray parameter: exact coincident twins explain only tens per scan, and most flagged triangles stay flagged when cast from three other interior points, so they are real overlaps (differently triangulated doubled caps and doubled skin), not ray leaks.

MeshRepair stage 7 (pruneExposedFaces): on a closed filled surface, cast a ray from each face centroid against its normal (TriangleBvh.anyHit, parallel); delete every face whose ray escapes plus 2+round vertex rings round it, re-split, re-classify shells, refill; repeat (at most 16 rounds) until none escapes. Later rounds recast only faces whose remembered blocker died and the new fill. Stops if a refill leaves a loop open. Report gains exposedFaceCount, prunedFaceCount, pruneRoundCount, refilledHoleCount, refillOpenHoleCount; repair_mesh gains prune_exposed (default true). Not the ZGZ*16 arrangement: exact intersection resolution and per-cluster CDT on 1M-face scans was out of proportion; deleting exposed regions and refilling converges on all ten scans in 2-5 rounds.

Result (checking script, CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark): back-out / flaps 0 / 0 on all of IMG_4109-4118 (baseline 9824 / 1335). Faces pruned per scan 863 (4109) to 25070 (4117), all loops refilled. repair_mesh time before -> after (ms): 4109 2020->3523, 4110 2156->2994, 4111 1260->1926, 4112 1208->1985, 4113 2039->3229, 4114 1171->2895, 4115 1102->2011, 4116 1326->2850, 4117 2321->3514, 4118 1263->2495.

Reference rings vs CRAW-91 at this stack's base: IMG_4109 4 of 102 changed (1-2 edges), IMG_4110 11 of 72 (1-6 edges, except ring_57 193 -> 100 edges, a single-point plane ring whose section most likely ran round a pruned piece; not confirmed), IMG_4111 39 of 82 (0-15 edges). The IMG_4109 checked-in golden was already stale on master (fixture now has rings to ring_127). Goldens not re-accepted.

Known gap: the check casts along each face's own normal only; renders of the IMG_4113 eyes still show thin back-face specks along the rims from oblique views (tmp/craw-92-4113-eye-before/after.png). CoincidentAnchorSaveTest's nested-sphere fixture sets prune_exposed=false: its faceted inner sphere pokes through the outer at the welded pole, and pruning would cut the overlap the test holds rings on.

Stricter rule (user goal: zero flipped faces): a face counts as flipped when ANY of 25 rays into its back hemisphere escapes (the normal plus 8 rays on each of the 30/55/75-degree cones), not only the normal ray. The normal-ray-only stage left 1001 such faces over the ten scans (the IMG_4113 eye-rim specks). The stage now prunes by the hemisphere rule; to keep it fast it skips faces whose back cell has a nonzero winding number (TriangleBvh.agreedWinding: signed crossing count along the normal and one slanted ray, equal, no crossing within 1e-4), except slivers, faces under 1% of the mean area and faces with a corner neighbour folded back past ~105 degrees, which always cast all 25 rays; later rounds recount only faces whose counting rays meet a face that died or was added (dead faces' corners are copied before splitNonManifold renumbers vertices). anyHit walks the nearer box first, tolerates a 1e-9 barycentric slack at shared edges, and the stage's trees use 4-triangle leaves.

Result: CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark (now asserting all three counts) reports back-out 0, flaps 0, back seen at any slant 0 on every one of IMG_4109-4118. repair_mesh ms CRAW-91 -> now: 4109 2020->7187 (first scan, JIT warm-up), 4110 2156->4403, 4111 1260->3508, 4112 1208->4756, 4113 2039->8554, 4114 1171->3894, 4115 1102->2992, 4116 1326->4032, 4117 2321->5558, 4118 1263->3831. mvn test 761/0.

Open: IMG_4109 reference graph (fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl) no longer builds: spline_ring ring_22 is a plane ring placed on a small inside-out lump that the hemisphere rule now prunes (tmp/craw-92-4109-ring22-before/after.png), so the plane meets only a 4-point loop. Needs the user's decision: re-place ring_22 on the skin, or exempt it. IMG_4110: 19 of 72 rings changed (ring_57 193->98), IMG_4111: 43 of 82 (within 15 edges). The viewer's cyan rim specks are not a flipped-face map: mesh.fs lights (1 - viewNormal.z)^2 of the interpolated vertex normal, so creases glow on correctly wound faces.

Speed work (user target: repair_mesh under 1 s, after under 3 s): round 0 now reads each face's back-cell parity from TriangleBvh.facing (now parallel, with crowdMargin flagging lines that cross another sheet within 1e-4) instead of casting two full rays per face: round-0 ray work 0.86 s -> 0.35 s; still 0/0/0 on all ten scans. Warm per-stage ms (IMG_4115 / IMG_4113 / IMG_4117): orient 281/360/285, split 131/124/123, shells 132/152/141, fill 72/418/1302, assemble 286/293/274, pruning 1434/4149/1996; totals 2.4-5.6 s. Pruning's cost is per round: full-mesh tree rebuild ~120 ms, crease scan ~55, splitNonManifold ~100, classifyShells ~100, plus 25-ray tests on the 6k-38k creased/tiny/sliver faces. Under 1 s total also needs the pre-existing stages roughly halved (they alone are ~0.9-1.0 s warm on most scans, 2.2 s on IMG_4117 from fill). Temporary [tmp] stage timers are in MeshRepair while this continues.

Paused speed work (target: repair_mesh under 1 s per scan). Latest warm times, check still 0/0/0 on all ten: 4109 1.19 s, 4110 1.09, 4111 1.20, 4112 1.01, 4113 1.85, 4114 1.27, 4115 0.91, 4116 1.09, 4117 1.47, 4118 1.19. Done: persistent pruning tree with retired faces and a companion tree for refills; parity (parallel TriangleBvh.facing with crowdMargin) instead of per-face rays; per-face verdicts rechecked only when changed faces touch their evidence (column grid prefilter); parallel BVH build (opt-in parallelBuild), parallel buildColumns, parallel MeshRepair.buildEdges, parallel crease scan, local degenerate adjacency, parallel hole-fill DP and per-loop fills, SlotCarry edge trace only when edge slots exist, parallel HalfEdgeMeshOps.packedBuild (same output), local pinch split and debris drop after cuts. Left: orient ~0.2 s, base split ~0.1, base shells ~0.1, assemble ~0.1, pruning parity ~0.15 and 25-ray tests on creased faces (fold threshold just tightened to 120 degrees, check still 0). Uncommitted: temporary [tmp] timers/counters in MeshRepair, an over-indented block in TriangleBvh.fileAxisColumns; mvn test, goldens and ring_22 decision not redone since these changes.

Cold-start pass and cleanup (2026-11-02): edge table rebuilt as serial stable counting passes (first build ~210 ms -> ~75 ms cold); orientation flips patch the edge table instead of rebuilding it; half-edge build numbers edges in one serial pass and reads normals off the flat arrays (same arithmetic); shell containment casts rays only for shells the debris threshold keeps, in one pass over the faces, no tree; atomics removed from the crease, edge and half-edge passes; pruning builds its tree, parity and creases concurrently, orient files its columns while clusters grow; temporary timers and counters removed; dead TriangleBvh.positiveAxisRayCrossings removed. New CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark times a repair in one fresh JVM per scan. Results: CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark 0/0/0 on all ten scans; mvn test 761 run, 0 failures. Heavy goldens: the nine crawfish scan graphs fingerprint differently only by the pruning (faces drop by pruned minus refilled, boundary stays 0) and need the user's OK to re-bless (cp -r ixdar-app/target/golden-actual/. ixdar-app/test/resources/golden/); fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl fails at ring_22 (spline_ring: no spline on a 4-point loop) because ring_22 sits on a lump the stage prunes, decision pending with the user. Cold repair is still 3-5 s per scan; the redesign to bring it under 1 s is CRAW-93.

review-summary: MeshRepair gains a last stage that deletes faces whose back sees out along their normal, with a widening ring round them, and refills the holes until none is left. Folds poking through the skin and overlapping fills otherwise leave inside-out patches on every crawfish scan.
